newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ping-pong bombs wound four children in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Ping-pong bombs wound four children in Philippines.

text.p: Four children were injured in Iligan City in the southern Philippines when ping-pong balls they picked up exploded, police said on Friday.
Police said the ping-pong balls, which had been stuffed with gun powder by local hunters, were being dried under the sun when the children picked them up on Thursday.

One 10-year old boy lost eight fingers and suffered multiple wounds to his stomach. Doctors said he was now "out of danger". The other three children suffered shrapnel wounds and have been discharged from hospital.

Hunters use the "ping-pong bombs" to kill wild boar and deer in the nearby forests of Lanao del Sur and Lanao del Norte, police said. They place the bombs on the known pathways of boar and deer near streams.
The owner of the explosive ping-pong balls was being sought by police, said Iligan police chief Mariano Pagente.
